lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Ah, you again, splendid! On my rather <color=red>circuitous</color> walk this morning, I stumbled upon an old notebook of dinosaur riddles.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Solve all three, and three new books will be <color=red>dispatched</color> to the library. I'd solve them myself, but I've forgotten the answers, naturally.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 1: My name means 'three-horned face', and I wore a broad, bony <color=red>frill</color> behind my head. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which name begins with a prefix meaning 'three'?
lines.correctText: Correct. 'Tri' means three, as in Triceratops.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 2: I am no creature at all, but the <color=red>mineralised</color> remains of one, preserved in rock for millions of years until someone patiently brushes me free. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which of these is the preserved remains of a living thing?
lines.correctText: Precisely. A fossil is the preserved trace of ancient life.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 3: I hurtled in from space some sixty-six million years ago, and many scientists believe my impact led to the <color=red>extinction</color> of the dinosaurs. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which of these could arrive from space?
lines.correctText: Well reasoned. An asteroid, arriving from space.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Most <color=red>astute</color>, all three! Three new books are already on their way to the library, which is more than I can say for my spectacles.

afterLines.speaker: Old Barnaby
afterLines.text: I've been mulling over a fourth riddle, but it seems to have become rather <color=red>extinct</color> in my memory.
